basis: In 2025 the government strategy says the lack of an ICT strategy since 2017 leaves a significant institutional vacuum in digital transformation, while the Commission screening report says the country has a well-structured institutional set-up.

In 2025 the State Audit Office reports no established line of accountability and coordination between the digital ministry and the innovation fund, while the Commission reports a well-structured institutional set-up for digital policy.

In 2022 the ITU says a National ICT council of ministers monitors sector ICT projects and ensures coherence across institutions, while the State Audit Office reports no government body coordinating and monitoring systems shared by several institutions.

In July 2023 the government strategy says digital transformation is perhaps the only area with no institution competent for implementation, while the Commission says the ministry is tasked to lead on all digitalisation projects.

In 2025 the State Audit Office says personal data protection in AI projects is regulated by legislation aligned with European standards, especially the GDPR, while the Commission says adoption of legislation to fully align with the GDPR is still pending.

In 2025 North Macedonia states it is aligned with the acquis on the use of digital tools and processes in company law, while the Commission says further alignment on the use of digital tools and processes is necessary.

The 2024 audit says citizens receive electronic documents in the electronic mailbox of the national portal, while the 2025 government strategy says the ministry will develop an electronic mailbox and integrate it into the portal.
In 2022 both describe the unadopted ICT strategy, but the Commission gives its period as 2021-2026 and the State Audit Office gives it as 2021-2025.
A research institute and the State Audit Office both state that the country lacks specific legislation on AI; the research paper cites the audit elsewhere, so independence on this point is partial.
A research institute and the Commission both state that North Macedonia needs to align with the EU AI Act.
The Commission and the State Audit Office both state in 2024 that the long-term ICT strategy and the national cybersecurity strategy had not been adopted.
The Commission and the State Audit Office both describe the digitalisation of public services as fragmented across institutions.
The government strategy and the Commission both state that the rules did not cover the archiving of electronic documents before the 2025 law.
The World Bank and the Commission both state in 2024 that digitalisation of businesses is low.
The World Bank and the government strategy both state that small businesses have low understanding of digital technologies.
The Commission and the government strategy both state that low digital skills hold back domestic businesses.
The World Bank and the Commission both describe e-commerce in the country as underdeveloped or growing slowly.
North Macedonia, as reported in the screening report, and the Commission in its 2025 report both state that national law is not yet aligned with the Digital Services Act and the Digital Markets Act.
North Macedonia, as reported in the screening report, and the Commission in its 2025 report both state that company formation and filing can be done fully online through the Central Registry.
